items.body: The specified witness cannot reproduce the existing goldens. Current `expected/rows.snap.txt` includes ScheduleToStart and StartToClose edges reaching TimedOut. R4 selects a world with no timeouts, and R5 disables Tick there. Adding `attempt` and action inputs also changes the state/action renderings pinned by those snapshots. The epic acknowledges this conflict but leaves the impossible acceptance criterion intact.
items.suggestion: Resolve the compatibility witness before the activity rewrite. State an executable check that satisfies the recorded compatibility decision, including deadline edges and rendering identity, and reconcile it across R4, R5 and task .3.
items.title: The specified witness cannot reproduce the existing goldens

items.body: Task .5 still instructs the implementer to read cancellation type from Start options. The current Start request mirror has no such field, and the epic explicitly confirms that neither the request nor standalone SDK options supplies it. Consequently, the task cannot construct `asynchronous_cancel` from its stated evidence without inventing a value or source.
items.suggestion: Identify the authorized evidence source and its transport before task .5, then update its construction contract and tests. Merely recording this as an open question does not make the current construction instruction executable.

items.body: The task requires reading an observed Start request but defines no route for delivering it. `Observation` contains only method and response/error; `StartActivityExecutionResponse` supplies no activity options. Furthermore, `Realize::observe` cannot replace the runtime’s private machine, and `Runtime::prepare` discards transactions on refusals. Implementing the task as a realization mapper cannot install the selected World or return Unsupported while committing the required freeze. The epic’s transactional-admission requirements are absent from the task’s approach and acceptance controls.
items.suggestion: Specify how the actual request and successful result reach admission within the envelope constraint. Carry World installation, exploration invalidation, admission-specific freezing and publication rollback into task .5, with controls for failed starts, failed publication and subsequent operations.

items.body: The task requires an expired-deadline fact without defining or assigning the necessary authoring support. Generated machines currently hard-code `Fact = ()`, require handlers to return nothing, and emit empty fact vectors. The lifter likewise emits `__umpire_facts' = <<>>`. Changing only the activity state and handlers cannot meet R5; emitting facts only natively also breaks backend replay’s outcome/fact comparison.
items.suggestion: Specify the narrow deadline-fact authoring contract and include its macro, source-lowering and replay work. Require matching native/TLC facts for each expiration and empty facts for ordinary transitions.
items.title: The task requires an expired-deadline fact without defining or assigning the necessary authoring support

items.body: Task .4 introduces `Option<Ticks>` and requires TLC verification, but no task specifies their source representation or expression lowering. The current lifter admits scalar integers, bools, fieldless enums and vectors; `Environment::ty` refuses `Option<Ticks>`. Task .7 binds values using that existing representation, while .2’s native range-newtype support does not establish optional-value lifting. Following the stated approaches leaves the timeout Model refused by TLC.
items.suggestion: Assign the concrete `Option<Ticks>` admission, binding, expression and decoding behavior within the existing tasks, with None/Some backend controls. Define the bounded tick representation without introducing general-purpose algebraic-type support.
